items.name: GD·00 Rules · API budgets
items.what: Every morning compares each paid API's month-to-date spend with its budget, alerts Tolu at 80% and sets the engine's pause switch at 100%.
setup: Select your Postgres credential "Supabase Postgres" (Supabase → Connect → Session pooler host, user, password) in every Postgres node; create the tables named in the sticky note first.
Select a Telegram credential (Tolu's approval bot) in the Telegram nodes and replace YOUR_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID with Tolu's chat ID.

Create api_budgets with one row per paid API, e.g. ('places', 30000, 'outreach_paused'), ('x', 15000, 'posting_paused'), ('ai', 40000, ''). Make each engine log spend as events with event 'api_usage' or 'ai_usage' and detail {api, channel, cost_ngn}.
Set Settings → Error workflow to your error workflow (HL·00 Errors from 6.4, or 3.6), then publish.
items.test: Insert test api_usage events adding up to 85% of the places budget and run it: Tolu gets one 80% alert and a budget_alert event; run again: no repeat. Push it past 100%: outreach_paused becomes true.

items.name: GD·01 Find · research, draft, approve
items.what: Weekday mornings: finds restaurants and hotels in the zone with Google Places, reads their websites, keeps only facts that appear word for word on the page, scores fit in code, drafts and lints a short email, and asks Tolu to approve each one on Telegram.
setup: Select your Postgres credential "Supabase Postgres" (Supabase → Connect → Session pooler host, user, password) in every Postgres node; create the tables named in the sticky note first.
Select a Telegram credential (Tolu's approval bot) in the Telegram nodes and replace YOUR_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID with Tolu's chat ID.
Create an OpenAI credential and select it in the model sub-node(s); replace YOUR_MODEL with a model you choose (small and cheap for labelling).
Your n8n must be reachable at a public HTTPS address (YOUR_N8N_DOMAIN) so Telegram approval buttons and webhooks work.
Create a Header Auth credential "Google Places": Name X-Goog-Api-Key, Value your Places API key, and select it in "Places Text Search". Set a budget alert in Google Cloud too.
Edit the areas in "Search areas" and the zone and ICP points in "Verify fact and score"; replace the signature name and domain in "Lint draft" with your own (keep the STOP line).
Adjust the per-call cost in "Log Places cost" to your field mask's price.
Set Settings → Error workflow to your error workflow (HL·00 Errors from 6.4, or 3.6), then publish.
items.test: Run it once with a single area and your own test business page (test 1): a prospect whose site has no usable fact gets the general first line, nothing invented, and waits for Approve on Telegram; Approve sets status approved, Skip sets skipped.

items.name: GD·01 Find · send approved (max 20 a day)

items.test: From a test account comment "how much for a basket?" on Instagram (test 3): a private reply with today's price, a short public note, and a lead row with source instagram. A Facebook comment 9 days old asking for supply gets a public reply only and a lead (test 4). A spam comment with a link is hidden with no reply (test 6). Empty the week in a test copy: Tolu gets the alarm instead.

walk.title: Build it: the growth report that answers the investor
walk.sample: Test week · an Instagram comment "how much for a basket?" becomes a lead, and that customer pays a test order on Thursday

steps.say: Six engines feed this report: find, listen, publish, answer, unify and nurture. Tolu's rule holds across all of them: anything that spends money, promises something or talks to an angry customer comes to her first.
show: GD·01–06 log events with lead_id or order_id
Budgets alert at 80%; pause switches at 100%

steps.say: Every Monday at 8, GD·07 answers the investor's question: where do customers come from, and what does each one cost?
One query reads the shared Supabase record. New customers are counted by first-touch source, set once when the customer was created, from their first paid order.
It also gets conversion from lead to first order over 90 days, and the median first reply time per channel, with complaints measured separately.
show: replies: median minutes per channel and kind

steps.say: Costs include the ones on no invoice: API and AI usage events, a weekly share of fixed plans, and Tolu's approval minutes at her hourly value.
From the CRM we read the pipeline's stages and win chances, through the private app token in an n8n credential.
Then all open deals, so the report can show value by stage. The report only reads; people move deals.
Code calculates every number: cost per lead and per new customer by channel, the overall cost, and the weighted forecast, each deal's value times its win chance.
If there were no leads, customers or events all week, that's not a quiet week, it's a broken engine. So no report goes out.
Tolu gets an alarm instead, pointing her to the watchdog and the error workflow.
show: Growth report NOT sent … That's an alarm

steps.say: The AI adds one recommendation, quoting the numbers exactly as given. It may not calculate or invent any. Code counts; AI explains.
show: One or two sentences: move time or money

steps.say: We assemble one page: new customers by first touch, conversion, reply times, cost per customer, pipeline and forecast, complaints and unsubscribes.
show: By first touch · Lead → first order
Median first reply · Cost per new customer

steps.say: It goes to Tolu on Telegram, and by email for the full copy.
Finally we log success as an event, so the watchdog knows GD·07 ran. Attach the error workflow before you publish.

walk.end: Run it by hand on the test week: Instagram shows under first touch with a cost per new customer, the pipeline has a weighted forecast, and an empty week sends the alarm instead.

note: GD·07 Growth report and GD·08 CRM sync (upsert, stage follow-ups, morning list, Ops Agent and executor) are built in full; GD·01–GD·06 follow the boss brief and the 5.2–5.7 solved builds, and GD·00 covers the API budgets from D1. All engines share one Supabase database (Postgres credential) and write events with lead_id or order_id. For the error workflow and watchdog that must cover every engine, use HL·00 Errors and HL·00 Watchdog from 6.4. The channel-rules sheet, consent policy, Brevo automations (welcome, win-back) and domain authentication are set up outside n8n.
